# Suites that do not pass, with the reason each one fails.
#
# These are NOT harness gaps. Every one of them was merged without ever being
# executed, because `supabase/tests/*.sql` ran in no CI job — so nothing ever
# told anyone. The first run of this harness is the first time any of them has
# been executed at all.
#
# They are quarantined rather than fixed here because fixing them is test-
# authoring work with real judgement in it (what did the author intend to
# assert?), and bundling fifteen of those into a CI-infrastructure change would
# make both harder to review. Quarantining keeps the gate live for the eleven
# suites that DO pass and for the migration chain itself, which is the part
# that protects the next migration.
#
# THE LIST IS SELF-CLEANING: a suite named here that starts PASSING fails the
# build, with a message telling you to delete the line. It cannot rot into a
# permanent ignore-list.
#
# Format: one filename per line. `#` comments and blank lines ignored.

# The six "branch_id => gen_random_uuid()" suites were here. Each now inserts
# its own branch row and references it, so orders_branch_id_fkey is satisfied
# by a branch that actually exists. Fixed, not quarantined.

# The profile-fixture suites were here. Each now creates the auth.users row
# before the profile (profiles.id references auth.users(id)) and upserts the
# profile, because handle_new_user() has already created it from that insert.
# discounts_campaigns and order_confirmation_state_machine now PASS.
#
# discounts_campaigns, order_confirmation_state_machine, loyalty_reason_*
# and order_read_contracts all pass now. The last three needed one more
# fixture row each: a branch behind v_branch, an order behind the loyalty
# transaction, and an auth user behind the customer.

# --- Genuine assertion failures, worth investigating on their own merits -----

# require_address_description_test.sql was here. It was right: btrim's default
# character set is a space and ONLY a space, so a landmark of tabs and
# newlines measured 5 characters and qualified. Fixed by migration
# 20260802120000_address_description_trim_all_whitespace.sql, so the suite is
# no longer quarantined.

# operations_alerts_activation_test.sql was here, failing on "expected exactly
# 5 cron jobs total". The comment used to leave two possibilities open; it was
# the first of them. The chain schedules seven jobs on a clean database and the
# suite had simply never been updated:
#   account-deletion-processor    20260716180000
#   lazywait-sync                 20260720120000
#   order-integrity-watchdog      20260721170000
#   operations-alerts-evaluator   20260723120000  <- this suite's own feature
#   operations-digest-generator   20260723120000  <- this suite's own feature
#   payment-refund-worker         20260729090000
#   branch-availability-sweep     20260820111000
#
# So 5 was right the day it was written, and every unrelated feature that adds
# a cron job broke it again. The total-count assertion is gone; the suite now
# asserts that each of the five jobs it knows about exists exactly once on its
# own schedule with its own command, and the existing scan over every cron
# command for credentials or outbound calls is untouched. Fixed, not
# re-quarantined.

# STATUS products.total — assertion about a products column.
lazywait_mapping_test.sql

# READONLY FAILED: vault.decrypted_secrets.decrypted_secret must be read-only.
# The harness view now makes that column non-updatable, so the remaining
# failure is a later case in the same file. Needs the full error re-read once
# the earlier cases are addressed.
lazywait_sync_scheduler_test.sql
